mission: HEADROOM PHASE-3 - AUTHENTICATED EVIDENCE UNIVERSE CONSISTENCY AUDIT (semantic accountability vs numeric grounding)
headline: There is no production semantic-accountability attribution check. The historical `attribution.unsourced: ["100%"]` was produced by a FORENSIC HARNESS function that nothing else in the repository consumes, and no benchmark or scoring path takes an IR-to-source attribution input of any kind. The architectural discrepancy the mission suspected is therefore not where it was expected - but two real ones were found in its place.

attributionTrace.valueExtraction: assertedAmounts() at span-validation.ts:64 - regex /\$[\d,]{4,}|\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?%/g over JSON.stringify({rules, definitions}); it reads the WHOLE serialized IR including provenance excerpts, and recognizes only $-amounts and percentages
attributionTrace.evidenceSearch: plain substring containment (after whitespace normalization) in exactly two strings: anchorText = index.getNodeText(structuralNodeIds[0], 'DESCENDANTS'), and parentText = the Pass C linked nodes' DESCENDANTS text (span-validation.ts:123)
attributionTrace.classification: supportedByAnchor / violations (in the linked material only) / unsourced (in neither). There is no third bucket - tool-retrieved evidence cannot be expressed at all
attributionTrace.accountabilityResult: none - the value is written into a forensic JSON report and consumed by nothing
attributionTrace.consumers: grep over lib/, app/ and tests/ for attributionCheck | unsourced | assertedAmounts returns ZERO hits outside span-validation.ts and span-validation-b2.ts

productionAccountabilityDirection.finding: Production semantic accountability runs SOURCE -> IR, never IR -> SOURCE.
evidence: INVENTORY_DISPOSITIONS (REPRESENTED / INTENTIONALLY_NON_COMPUTATIONAL / UNSUPPORTED / AMBIGUOUS / MISSING_FROM_COMPOSITION) are dispositions OF A SOURCE INVENTORY ITEM - 'UNSUPPORTED' means the composition consumed the source item into an UNSUPPORTED node, not that the model asserted something unsupported

computeSourceCoverage asks whether every stretch of the candidate's own source REGION is accounted for; its universe is SourceContextRegion[] (OPERATIVE, CROSS_REFERENCE_EXPANSION, ENCLOSING_NODE_EXPANSION) resolved from the structural index
the compiler prompt's own accountability clause is phrased entirely in the source->IR direction, including 'additional deterministically-detected values ... must be represented'
no check anywhere asks whether an IR node lacks inventory lineage
productionAccountabilityDirection.consequence: Accountability cannot call an assertion - numeric or qualitative - unsourced, because it never grades assertions. The only production IR->source checks are the verifier's findIrOnlyNumericItems (structured) and Fix B (free-text).

reconstructedHistoricalCondition.note: the original run's IR is lost, so '100%' was injected into this run's own real rule field to reproduce the observed condition - labelled as a reconstruction, not as the original
reconstructedHistoricalCondition.theFlip: YES - '100%' flips out of UNSOURCED once authenticated tool retrieval is admitted
reconstructedHistoricalCondition.butAlsoRevealing: under view B the harness moves it into 'violations' rather than a grounded bucket, because attributionCheck has only two buckets and cannot express tool-retrieved evidence. Widening that function's inputs alone would replace one wrong label with another.

replay_7_2_f.groundingSource: toolCallLog[0] getDefinition{term:'Subsidiary Guarantor'} -> retrievedSource.rawText = '"Subsidiary Guarantor": (a) each Material Domestic Subsidiary and (b) each Material Foreign Subsidiary that is a Pledge Eligible Foreign Subsidiary (100%).', charStart 42258, charEnd 42415, contentHash e0ae4ef9188e..., evidenceStatus CURRENT, evidenceUnresolved false, textOrigin BASE_DOCUMENT_TEXT

corpusInterpretation.headline: Zero ACCOUNTABILITY_ONLY_GROUNDED across the whole corpus: the historical universe never grounds anything Fix B does not. It is strictly narrower.
corpusInterpretation.theFourDisagreements: All four are FIX_B_ONLY_GROUNDED and all four are NORMALIZED_EQUIVALENT in the OPERATIVE window - not a tool-retrieval issue at all. The source writes '$50\u00a0million' and '$115\u00a0million' (with a non-breaking space); the IR asserts '$50,000,000' and '$115,000,000'. A substring test calls that unsourced; Fix B's scale-aware canonicalization grounds it correctly in the candidate's own anchor.
corpusInterpretation.toolEvidenceCoverage: only 4 of 171 preserved compilation sites carry authenticated tool rawText at all, so the corpus can say very little about the tool-retrieval channel specifically - the 7.2(f) replay is the direct evidence there
corpusInterpretation.insufficientArtifacts: 103 of 133 assertions were not gradeable because the artifact preserved compiled rules without the source text they came from

creditSemantics.why: the signal has no consumer: grep for attributionCheck/unsourced/assertedAmounts outside the two harness scripts returns nothing, and evaluation-v2 / benchmark scoring take no IR->source attribution input at all
creditSemantics.consequence: the too-narrow universe made the COMPILER LOOK WORSE IN A FORENSIC REPORT, and misled two missions, but it never cost the pipeline a single point of credit

falseCreditAnalysis.measurement: Fix B was tested against its own weakness on the real 7.2(f) input and its real authenticated evidence: an assertion genuinely about the retrieved definition ('may cover up to 100% of the obligations of any Subsidiary Guarantor') and an assertion that has nothing to do with it ('may prepay up to 100% of the outstanding Revolving Loans') BOTH return GROUNDED_CONTEXT with zero findings.
falseCreditAnalysis.conclusion: Fix B's relation is 'this figure occurs in authenticated source', which is exactly right for its own job - catching a figure supported by NOTHING - and is NOT strong enough to carry attribution credit.
falseCreditAnalysis.contrastWithTheStructuredPath: reconciliation.ts's irItemScopedToEvidence already imposes the stricter relation for STRUCTURED numerics: retrieved evidence may support an IR value only when that value is scoped to it (the item belongs to that term's IRDefinition, or its own citation names that definition/section). Fix B deliberately does not, and the two are therefore inconsistent with each other.
risksIfAttributionWereWidenedNaively: a retrieved definition is misapplied to the wrong proposition
a retrieved sibling basket's threshold is attributed to the current clause - precisely the attribution class candidate-span/F1 exists to prevent
a cross-reference figure is used for a different proposition
the same figure appears in several retrieved results and any of them 'supports' it

rootCause.primary: 7_2_F_HARNESS_ONLY_DEFECT - the false UNSOURCED came from a forensic harness function with a two-string evidence universe and a substring test, not from any production accountability path.
secondary: ACCOUNTABILITY_EVIDENCE_UNIVERSE_TOO_NARROW, in the narrow sense that applies: the harness check omitted BOTH authenticated tool retrieval AND rendering equivalence. Production accountability is not too narrow because it does not perform attribution at all - which is itself the gap.

FIX_B_EVIDENCE_UNIVERSE_TOO_BROAD for attribution purposes: it matches a figure anywhere in authenticated evidence, with no semantic relation to the assertion, unlike the structured path's irItemScopedToEvidence.
RENDERING_EQUIVALENCE_GAP: 4 of 4 corpus disagreements are '$50 million' vs '$50,000,000', independent of any tool channel.
NO_IR_TO_SOURCE_QUALITATIVE_CHECK: nothing anywhere grades a qualitative assertion against evidence, so qualitative false-unsourced cannot occur - and neither can qualitative fabrication detection.

remediationDesign.required: YES, but not where the mission expected, and not urgently - nothing is scoring wrong today
remediationDesign.R1_harness: Retire attributionCheck's two-string universe. Have the forensic runners call Fix B's groundNumericAssertions against the authenticated evidence set instead of re-implementing a weaker test. Smallest possible change, removes a whole class of misleading forensic output, touches no production code.
remediationDesign.R2_fixB_relation: Give Fix B the same scoping discipline the structured path already has: a free-text assertion may be GROUNDED_CONTEXT by a retrieved definition only when the owning rule/condition's own citation names that definition or section, or the assertion's field belongs to that definition's unit. Anything else becomes a new, weaker status rather than full grounding.
remediationDesign.statusVocabulary: GROUNDED_OPERATIVE / GROUNDED_CONTEXT / GROUNDED_TOOL_EVIDENCE / UNSOURCED / AMBIGUOUS - do NOT collapse. The existing NumericGroundingStatus union already carries GROUNDED_OPERATIVE, GROUNDED_CONTEXT, NORMALIZED_EQUIVALENT, UNGROUNDED and AMBIGUOUS, and `groundedIn` already separates OPERATIVE from CONTEXT. Adding GROUNDED_TOOL_EVIDENCE (or, equivalently, extending groundedIn with TOOL_RETRIEVAL) is a two-value additive change - the types can express the distinction with no restructuring.
remediationDesign.invariantToPreserve: authenticated tool-retrieved source may SUPPORT an assertion through its actual source channel and semantic relationship, and is never promoted to anchor-owned operative evidence
remediationDesign.typeChangesRequired: MINIMAL AND ADDITIVE - one new enum member on an existing union, or one new value on groundedIn
remediationDesign.fixBChangeRequired: YES for R2, and it TIGHTENS rather than widens - it cannot create false credit
